chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who circumambulates the House and [performs the walk] between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa is released [from Ihram], whether he likes it or not.'

key_terms.أَحَبَّ أَوْ كَرِهَ: Whether he liked it or not (indicating automatic effect)
key_terms.أَحَلَّ: Was released/free (from the restrictions of Ihram)
key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa (one of the hills in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: When does a pilgrim become free from Ihram during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of exiting the state of Ihram for Mufrid and Qarin pilgrims, establishing that the completion of Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'i serves as the definitive act of release (Halal), irrespective of whether the pilgrim explicitly intended to perform these rites or did so incidentally. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the objective nature of ritual completion over subjective intent for this specific stage, distinguishing it from the initial entry into Ihram. The narration highlights the reliability of the chain through Zurarah, a key companion of Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq, reinforcing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt's legal teachings.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying: ‘The one who circumambulates with the House (Kabah), and with Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, is free (from Ihraam), whether he likes it or not’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following: “
I once heard Abu `Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, £ One who performs Tawaf around the House and al-Safa’ and al-Marwah is out of the state of Ihram, whether he likes or not.’”
